label: Foreign resident: years of Korean residence triggering full worldwide taxation
unit: years of residence within the preceding 10
appliesTo: Foreign nationals who are Korean tax residents and hold foreign-source income
why: The exception that stops 'resident means worldwide income' being true for most foreign arrivals, and the one most often missed. It is cumulative across ten years, so it changes silently as a stay lengthens rather than on any single date.

history.display: 5 years or less, in the preceding 10
history.source: Income Tax Act — scope of taxation for foreign residents
history.note: A foreign resident whose Korean residence within the ten years to the end of the tax period totals five years or less is taxed on foreign-source income only to the extent it is paid in Korea or remitted to Korea. Beyond that threshold the ordinary worldwide basis matters much more. Counted cumulatively, so it needs tracking year by year rather than checking once.
